Prevention: Buy and plant certified resistant varieties such as
Mamaba from reputable source (registered certified seed dealers).
Use recommended spacing of the maize (80x40cm) and recommended fertilizer rates (4bags or 200kg of
NPK 15:15:15 per ha) to increase the growth vigor
Plant maize early in the major and minor seasons and avoid staggered planting
Maize with legumes such as beans, cowpeas and soyabean

Weed the maize and clear the grass around the maize crop and maintain a barrier of 10m bare ground between plot and the sourrounding crop or weeds to reduce the vector (leaf hoppers) population and disease transmission
Monitoring: Maize streak is a virus disease transmitted by plant hoppers and leaf hoppers
Scout frequently for leafhoppers and disease symptoms starting 1 week after germination if the virus is known from your area
Plants infected with maize streak virus show symptoms 10 to 14 days after infection
Symptoms appear mostly on young growing tender leaves, which are preferred by leafhoppers for feeding
Symptoms vary from clear narrow light green to mild chlorotic streaks centred on secondary and tertiary leaf veins.
They are uniformly distributed on the leaf surface thus cannot be mistaken with other diseases.
Parallel yellow streaks appear and the plants remain stunted, producing small ears
Consider control when 1-3 leaf hoppers (vectors) are seen per maize plant or if early symptoms of the disease are seen
Direct Control: Uproot / rogue infected maize plants when they first show signs of disease to avoid the disease from spreading to healthy plants.
Put the whole plant in a sack so the leaf hoppers do not go to other plants then destroy by burning or feed to livestock
Weed and remove grasses from the maize field to reduce vector population
Control the vector (leaf hoppers) which transmit the virus with insecticides
Applied at a rate of 60-70mls per 15 lts knapsack sprayer.
A contact and ingested organophosphorus insecicide; IRAC mode of action 1B
Deltamethrin based products (check product label for the recommended dosage).
Pyrethroid with a contact and stomach poison or with residual activity (i.e. 3-4 weeks persistence).
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
There are no pesticides for the virus but insecticides can be used to reduce the insect vector that spreads the disease
II (Moderately hazardous), pre-harvest interval p.h.i. 35 days; restricted re-entry interval r.e.i. 3 days.
Repeat application max twice if the pests/ vectors persist and reach thresholds.
Apply early morning or late afternoon.

High risk predators, pollinators, to fish and other aquatic organisms.
Do not contaminate surface waters or ditches; do not apply to plants suffering from drought or other physical distress; do not spray within 6m of field boundary.
